We've established that the strongest transcriptional signal (HRD vs HRP) comes from chemokines, but as this is closely correlated with tumour purity it is clearly coming from the tumour microenvironment.

The tumour -intrinsic signal is thus likely weak. So we need to design a new DE-GSEA analysis where we control for microenvironmental factors and work only with high purity samples.

```{r}
## design
design <- model.matrix(~ tumorPurity + score_stroma + score_blood + HRD_status, 
                       data = meta_unique_rna_all)

## high purity
dat_high <- meta_unique_rna_all %>% filter(tumorPurity > 0.6)
```

```{r}
DNAvsRNA_ti <- function(pats = NULL,            # optional: user-supplied altered patients
                     gene,
                     counts,
                     pws,
                     metadata,              # NEW: must contain id_col + purity_col
                     id_col     = "patientID",
                     purity_col = "tumorPurity",
                     use_cnv = FALSE,        # TRUE to also include CNV deletions
                     purity_df = 3,          # 1 = linear purity, >1 spline
                     logFC_cutoff = 1.5,
                     fdr_cutoff   = 0.01,
                     top_n        = 20,
                     minSize      = 15,
                     maxSize      = 500,
                     run_ssgsea   = TRUE,    # NEW
                     ssgsea_alpha = 0.25,    # NEW
                     ssgsea_norm  = TRUE     # NEW
) {
  
  ## 0. Basic checks
  if (length(gene) != 1) stop("DNAvsRNA() only accepts a single gene symbol.")
  if (missing(pws) || is.null(pws)) stop("Please provide a named list of pathways in 'pws'.")
  if (!is.list(pws) || is.null(names(pws))) stop("pws must be a *named list*.")
  if (missing(metadata) || is.null(metadata)) stop("Please provide 'metadata' with tumour purity.")
  if (!all(c(id_col, purity_col) %in% names(metadata)))
    stop("metadata must contain columns: ", paste(c(id_col, purity_col), collapse = ", "))
  
  ## 1. Choose altered patients
  if (is.null(pats)) {
    mut_pats <- get_mut_pats(gene)
    message("Using get_mut_pats(): ", length(mut_pats), " altered patients for ", gene)
  } else {
    mut_pats <- as.character(pats)
    message("Using user-supplied pats: ", length(mut_pats), " altered patients")
  }
  
  ## 2. Optionally add CNV-deleted patients
  if (use_cnv) {
    cnv_df   <- getCNV(gene, "DEL")
    cnv_pats <- unique(cnv_df$patientID)
    message("Adding ", length(cnv_pats), " CNV-del patients")
    mut_pats <- unique(c(mut_pats, cnv_pats))
  }
  
  ## 3. Define universe + groups
  all_pats <- colnames(counts)
  mut_pats <- intersect(mut_pats, all_pats)
  if (length(mut_pats) == 0) stop("No altered patients found in counts after matching IDs.")
  
  NON_mut_pats <- setdiff(all_pats, mut_pats)
  if (length(NON_mut_pats) == 0) stop("No non-altered patients left (NON_mut_pats empty).")
  
  message("Performing DE for ",
          length(mut_pats), " Alt vs ",
          length(NON_mut_pats), " WT patients")
  
  # Subset counts (genes x samples)
  count_df <- counts[, c(mut_pats, NON_mut_pats), drop = FALSE]
  
  # Group labels aligned to columns
  group <- factor(c(rep("T", length(mut_pats)),
                    rep("C", length(NON_mut_pats))))
  sample_ids <- colnames(count_df)
  
  # ---- Build sample_info aligned to count_df columns ----
  sample_info <- metadata[match(sample_ids, metadata[[id_col]]), , drop = FALSE]
  if (anyNA(sample_info[[id_col]])) {
    bad <- sample_ids[is.na(sample_info[[id_col]])]
    stop("These samples are missing from metadata (", id_col, "): ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "))
  }
  
  purity <- sample_info[[purity_col]]
  if (!is.numeric(purity)) stop(purity_col, " must be numeric in [0,1].")
  purity <- pmin(pmax(purity, 0), 1)
  sample_info$purity <- purity
  sample_info$group  <- group
  
  # ---- Purity-adjusted design for DE ----
  if (purity_df > 1) {
    design <- model.matrix(~ splines::ns(purity, df = purity_df) + group, data = sample_info)
  } else {
    design <- model.matrix(~ purity + group + score_stroma + score_blood, data = sample_info)
  }
  
  ## 4. edgeR DE (purity-adjusted)
  dge <- edgeR::DGEList(counts = count_df)
  keep <- edgeR::filterByExpr(dge, group = group)
  dge <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
  dge  <- edgeR::calcNormFactors(dge)
  ## exact normalised counts
  logCPM <- edgeR::cpm(dge, log = TRUE)
  
  message("Estimating dispersion")
  dge <- edgeR::estimateDisp(dge, design)
  fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(dge, design)
  qlf <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "groupT")
  
  DE  <- edgeR::topTags(qlf, n = nrow(dge$counts))
  res <- DE$table
  
  ## 5. Volcano plot
  res$gene   <- rownames(res)
  res$logFDR <- -log10(res$FDR)
  
  res$Significant <- "NS"
  res$Significant[res$logFC >  logFC_cutoff & res$FDR < fdr_cutoff] <- "Up"
  res$Significant[res$logFC < -logFC_cutoff & res$FDR < fdr_cutoff] <- "Down"
  
  sig_hits <- res[res$Significant != "NS", , drop = FALSE]
  
  Volcano <- ggplot2::ggplot(res, ggplot2::aes(x = logFC, y = logFDR)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(color = Significant), alpha = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(fdr_cutoff),
                        linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = c(-logFC_cutoff, logFC_cutoff),
                        linetype = "dotted", color = "black") +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c("Up"="#b2182b","Down"="#2166ac","NS"="#bdbdbd")) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data = sig_hits,
      ggplot2::aes(label = gene),
      max.overlaps = 30,
      size = 3,
      box.padding = 0.3,
      point.padding = 0.2,
      segment.color = "grey50"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = paste("Purity-adjusted DE:", length(mut_pats), "Alt vs WT for", gene),
      x = "Log2 Fold Change (Alt vs WT)",
      y = "-Log10 FDR"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  
  ## 6. Ranked list for fgsea (purity-adjusted because logFC is)
  gene_list <- res$logFC
  names(gene_list) <- rownames(res)
  gene_list <- sort(gene_list, decreasing = TRUE)
  gene_list_names <- names(gene_list)
  
  # Debug: pathway sizes & overlaps
  path_sizes   <- sapply(pws, length)
  path_overlap <- sapply(pws, function(g) length(intersect(gene_list_names, g)))
  
  fgseaRes <- fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(
    pathways = pws,
    stats    = gene_list,
    minSize  = minSize,
    maxSize  = maxSize
  )
  fgseaRes_df <- as.data.frame(fgseaRes)
  
  topPathways_df <- fgseaRes_df
  GSEA_plot <- NULL
  
  if (nrow(fgseaRes_df) > 0) {
    top_n2 <- min(top_n, nrow(fgseaRes_df))
    topPathways_df <- fgseaRes_df[order(fgseaRes_df$padj), ][1:top_n2, , drop = FALSE]
    
    topPathways_df$signif <- ifelse(topPathways_df$padj < fdr_cutoff, "Significant", "Not significant")
    topPathways_df$direction <- ifelse(topPathways_df$NES >= 0, "Up", "Down")
    topPathways_df$cat <- factor(
      paste(topPathways_df$direction, topPathways_df$signif, sep = "_"),
      levels = c("Up_Significant","Up_Not significant","Down_Significant","Down_Not significant")
    )
    
    GSEA_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(topPathways_df,
                                 ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(pathway, NES), y = NES, fill = cat)) +
      ggplot2::geom_col() +
      ggplot2::coord_flip() +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = "Pathway",
        y = "NES",
        title = paste("Purity-adjusted pre-ranked fgsea for", gene, "(Alt vs WT)")
      ) +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c("Up_Significant"="#b2182b","Up_Not significant"="#f4a582",
                   "Down_Significant"="#2166ac","Down_Not significant"="#92c5de"),
        labels = c("Up_Significant"="Up (padj<0.05)","Up_Not significant"="Up (NS)",
                   "Down_Significant"="Down (padj<0.05)","Down_Not significant"="Down (NS)")
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      ggplot2::theme(
        legend.title       = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
      )
  } else {
    warning("fgsea returned no pathways (likely low overlap or minSize too high).")
  }
  
  ## 7. ssGSEA (compute scores) + purity-adjusted Alt vs WT on scores
  ssgsea_scores <- ssgsea_de <- ssgsea_plot <- NULL
  
  if (run_ssgsea) {
    # log1p-CPM for ssGSEA (TMM), using the same samples
    y <- edgeR::DGEList(count_df)
    y <- edgeR::calcNormFactors(y, method = "TMM")
    expr_for_ssgsea <- log1p(edgeR::cpm(y, log = FALSE))  # genes x samples
    
    # ssGSEA
    par_ssgsea <- GSVA::ssgseaParam(
      exprData  = expr_for_ssgsea,
      geneSets  = pws,
      minSize   = 5,
      maxSize   = 5000,
      alpha     = ssgsea_alpha,
      normalize = ssgsea_norm
    )
    ssgsea_scores <- GSVA::gsva(par_ssgsea, verbose = FALSE)  # pathways x samples
    
    # Purity-adjusted model on pathway scores
    if (purity_df > 1) {
      design_ss <- model.matrix(~ splines::ns(purity, df = purity_df) + group, data = sample_info)
    } else {
      design_ss <- model.matrix(~ purity + group, data = sample_info)
    }
    
    fit_ss <- limma::lmFit(ssgsea_scores, design_ss)
    fit_ss <- limma::eBayes(fit_ss)
    
    ssgsea_de <- limma::topTable(fit_ss, coef = "groupT", number = Inf, sort.by = "P")
    ssgsea_de$pathway <- rownames(ssgsea_de)
    
    # Simple plot: top pathways by p-value (t-stat direction)
    top_show <- head(ssgsea_de, min(top_n, nrow(ssgsea_de)))
    ssgsea_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(top_show,
                                   ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(pathway, t), y = t)) +
      ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#1F77B4") +
      ggplot2::coord_flip() +
      ggplot2::labs(
        x = "Pathway",
        y = "t-stat (Alt vs WT, purity-adjusted)",
        title = "ssGSEA pathway differences (purity-adjusted Alt vs WT)"
      ) +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
  }
  
  ## 8. Return everything
  list(
    gene            = gene,
    mut_pats        = mut_pats,
    NON_mut_pats    = NON_mut_pats,
    sample_info     = sample_info,
    logCPM          = logCPM,
    DE_res          = res,
    Vol             = Volcano,
    GSEA            = topPathways_df,
    GSEA_plot       = GSEA_plot,
    pathway_sizes   = path_sizes,
    pathway_overlap = path_overlap,
    ssgsea_scores   = ssgsea_scores,
    ssgsea_de       = ssgsea_de,
    ssgsea_plot     = ssgsea_plot
  )
}
```

```{r}
HR_DE_GSEA <- DNAvsRNA(pats = hr_def_pats,  
                      gene = "HR",
                      counts = counts,
                      pws = pws,
                      metadata = meta_high_purity, 
                      id_col     = "hmfPatientId",
                      purity_col = "tumorPurity",
                      use_cnv = FALSE,        # TRUE to also include CNV deletions
                      purity_df = 3,          # 1 = linear purity, >1 spline
                      logFC_cutoff = 1.5,
                      fdr_cutoff   = 0.01,
                      top_n        = 30,
                      minSize      = 15,
                      maxSize      = 500,
                      run_ssgsea   = TRUE,    # NEW
                      ssgsea_alpha = 0.25,    # NEW
                      ssgsea_norm  = TRUE     # NEW
)
```

```{r}
high_purity_pats <- dat_high$hmfPatientId
high_purity_HRDpats <- hr_def_pats[hr_def_pats %in% high_purity_pats]
high_purity_counts <- counts[, colnames(counts) %in% high_purity_pats]
meta_high_purity <- meta_unique_rna_all[meta_unique_rna_all$hmfPatientId %in% 
                                          high_purity_pats, ]
## tumour intrinsic (ti)
HR_DE_GSEA_ti <- DNAvsRNA(pats = high_purity_HRDpats,  
                      gene = "HR",
                      counts = high_purity_counts,
                      pws = pws,
                      metadata = meta_high_purity, 
                      id_col     = "hmfPatientId",
                      purity_col = "tumorPurity",
                      use_cnv = FALSE,        # TRUE to also include CNV deletions
                      purity_df = 3,          # 1 = linear purity, >1 spline
                      logFC_cutoff = 1.5,
                      fdr_cutoff   = 0.01,
                      top_n        = 30,
                      minSize      = 15,
                      maxSize      = 500,
                      run_ssgsea   = TRUE,    # NEW
                      ssgsea_alpha = 0.25,    # NEW
                      ssgsea_norm  = TRUE     # NEW
)
```

```{r}
## RB1 loss still comes out top
# RB1
RB1_loss_up_LE_hp <- unlist(HR_DE_GSEA_ti$GSEA[1,8])

meta_high_purity <- meta_high_purity %>%
  mutate(
    HRD_status = if_else(hmfPatientId %in% hr_def_pats, "HRD", "HRP"),
    HRD_status = factor(HRD_status, levels = c("HRP", "HRD"))
  )

library(ggpubr)


```

```{r}
#### it seems clear that HRD is associated with an RB-loss transcriptional phenotype so the next question is, how much of this can be explained by the loss of TP53?

drivers_TP53 <- drivers_allIDs[drivers_allIDs$gene == "TP53", ] 
TP53_pats <- unique(drivers_TP53$hmfPatientId)

library(dplyr)

meta_high_purity <- meta_high_purity %>%
  mutate(
    TP53_status = if_else(hmfPatientId %in% TP53_pats, "alt", "wt"),
    TP53_status = factor(TP53_status, levels = c("wt", "alt"))
  )

ggplot(meta_high_purity, aes(TP53_status, RB1_loss_score, fill = TP53_status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
## there are more or less equal numberd of TP53 alt and wt patients in the HRD group, so what happens if we plot RB1_loss vs TP53 status just for those patients?

meta_HRD_highpur <- meta_high_purity[meta_high_purity$HRD_status == "HRD", ]

ggplot(meta_HRD_highpur, aes(TP53_status, RB1_loss_score, fill = TP53_status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
design <- model.matrix(~ HRD_status * TP53_status + tx_class + tumorPurity, data = meta_high_purity)
fit <- limma::lmFit(HR_DE_GSEA_ti$logCPM, design)
fit <- limma::eBayes(fit)
```

```{r}
## genes with an HRD effect after adjusting for TP53
library(limma)

res_hrd <- topTable(
  fit,
  coef = "HRD_statusHRD",
  number = Inf,
  sort.by = "P"
)

res_hrd$gene <- rownames(res_hrd)
head(res_hrd)
```

```{r}
res_int <- topTable(
  fit,
  coef = "HRD_statusHRD:TP53_statusalt",
  number = Inf,
  sort.by = "P"
)

res_int$gene <- rownames(res_int)
head(res_int)
```

```{r}
## let's try running a differential analysis between TP53 alt and wt in HRD patients

HRD_hp_counts <- counts[, colnames(counts) %in% high_purity_HRDpats]
HRD_TP53wt_hp <- meta_HRD_highpur[meta_HRD_highpur$TP53_status == "alt", ]
HRD_TP53wt_hp_pats <- unique(HRD_TP53wt_hp$hmfPatientId)

HR_DE_GSEA_ti_TP53 <- DNAvsRNA(pats = HRD_TP53wt_hp_pats,  
                      gene = "HR",
                      counts = HRD_hp_counts,
                      pws = pws,
                      metadata = meta_high_purity, 
                      id_col     = "hmfPatientId",
                      purity_col = "tumorPurity",
                      use_cnv = FALSE,        # TRUE to also include CNV deletions
                      purity_df = 3,          # 1 = linear purity, >1 spline
                      logFC_cutoff = 1.5,
                      fdr_cutoff   = 0.01,
                      top_n        = 30,
                      minSize      = 15,
                      maxSize      = 500,
                      run_ssgsea   = TRUE,    # NEW
                      ssgsea_alpha = 0.25,    # NEW
                      ssgsea_norm  = TRUE     # NEW
)
```

```{r}
HR_DE_ti_TP53 <- HR_DE_GSEA_ti_TP53$DE_res
```

```{r}
## conclusion: HRD does not define a separate transcriptional state — it defines a subtype within a TP53/RB-like proliferative state
```
